transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-28 14:00 PST | Duration: ~43m | Recording ID: rsf-20270328-0073
Attendees: Asha Malik (Redwood AE), Ryan Cho (Redwood SE), Leah Ortega (Redwood CSM), Omar Diaz (NorthStar), Priya Rao (NorthStar), Ben Turner (NorthStar), Maya Lin (NorthStar)

Summary: quick kickoff to align security, network, and expected throughput. customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Private, leaning toward Dedicated with VPC peering but need SOC2/ISO evidence and a latency proof point. action items and next steps captured.

Topics: onboarding timeline; security/compliance; network topology (VPC peering, proxies); benchmarks (p95/p99 latency, throughput); rollout plan (canary -> full); data retention and KMS; cost/commit sizing.

00:00:03 Asha: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick intros — i'll be the AE working with you, Ryan our solutions engineer and Leah our CSM will run the onboarding once we spin up.
00:00:18 Omar: Great thanks. we saw the deck you sent last night, thanks for that. we're mainly here to make sure security and ops are happy before we commit reserved capacity.
00:00:30 Asha: Totally. Goal for today is align on the technical intake items and agree next steps for a benchmark and security review.
00:00:45 Priya: i'll start - Security priorities: SOC2 evidence, encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, audit logs, and proof that no customer data leaves our region. also SSO/SAML and RBAC for console.
00:01:05 Ryan: Got it. Redwood supports KMS integrations and HSM workflows in Private and Dedicated. For the hosted API we have token-level controls, but for Dedicated you can bring your own keys via our KMS bridge. sometimes docs call it the K-M-S bridge in notes, apologies for naming drift.
00:01:35 Ben: what's the diff between Dedicated and Private in practice? we need the isolation but prefer not to self-manage.
00:01:50 Ryan: Short: Dedicated = reserved GPU pools managed by Redwood in your cloud region with VPC peering and isolated tenancy; Private = customer-managed control plane option or on-prem appliance where you control networking fully. Dedicated gives you less ops overhead.
00:02:10 Maya: OK, latency targets — our SLAs are 100ms p95 for short chat prompts and 250ms p95 for longer generation. will Redwood hit that?
00:02:28 Ryan: depends on model and quantization. for smaller models we see sub-100ms p95 on dedicated A100-style nodes for short seqs. for longer sequences p95 goes up. we'll run a benchmark with your sample workload to give realistic numbers.
00:02:50 Priya: Can we run the bench inside our VPC or do you need test traffic hitting Redwood endpoints? security prefers peered testing.
00:03:03 Ryan: we can do both. preferred is VPC peering with a dedicated test subnet and ephemeral keys so traffic never leaves your network fabric. we'll share a plan.
00:03:20 Asha: i'll follow up with a sample benchmark plan. Leah will kick off onboarding tickets.

00:03:40 Priya: Regarding data retention, we need confirmation that logs are only retained per our retention policy and ability to disable persistent prompt storage. is that configurable?
00:03:58 Leah: Yes, on Dedicated you can set retention rules per project and we have options to disable request storage; we'll provide the exact settings and screenshots in the runbook.
00:04:15 Omar: also curious about prefix/KV cache — we do a lot of session reuse for chat. do we worry about cross-tenant cache leakage?
00:04:30 Ryan: KV cache is shard-isolated per tenant in Dedicated. there's an option to pin KV to a tenant namespace; i'll include the architecture diagram. sometimes transcription calls it K-V cash in older notes — ignore that.

00:04:55 Ben: networking: we plan to peer a VPC in us-east-1 with your regional endpoint. what about egress/NAT? do you need any firewall rules?
00:05:10 Ryan: We only need a few CIDR ranges for the control plane to reach back for metrics and healthchecks when using the managed control plane. i'll attach a minimal firewall list. if you use Private, that traffic is internal.
00:05:30 Priya: we use strict egress rules. can Redwood support a proxy or transit gateway config?
00:05:40 Ryan: yes, proxy/proxyless is supported. We'll document the transit gateway pattern for peering.

00:06:05 Maya: for onboarding timeline — how long to stand up Dedicated capacity? we have a go-live goal mid-june.
00:06:18 Leah: Typically 4-6 weeks after contract and initial capacity sizing. if we start pre-provisioning with a commit we can shorten ramp. milestone plan: sizing -> bench -> canary -> rollout.
00:06:34 Omar: Our procurement window is 6 weeks, so timing is tight. we'll need the pricing sheet and a committed capacity proposal.
00:06:44 Asha: i'll share Dedicated pricing tiers and burst options. Ryan can size the initial reserved pool after the benchmark.

00:07:05 Priya: Audit logs and access controls: we need SSO, AD sync, and immutable audit logs exported to our SIEM (Splunk). what's the retention / export cadence?
00:07:20 Leah: Audit logs can be exported to S3 or your SIEM via secure syslog. retention configurable; we recommend 90 days by default, longer if required. we'll provide an example S3 lifecycle policy.

00:07:45 Ben: Are there pre-built alerts / tracing for token-level cost visibility? our finance team wants to track token spend by route.
00:07:58 Leah: Console has token-level billing breakdown, and we can provision a read-only billing view for finance. we can also pipe usage to your internal cost DB via daily export.

00:08:20 Maya: Model governance — can we pin model versions and rollback? we need deterministic outputs for enterprise features.
00:08:33 Ryan: Yes, model pinning and versioned rollouts supported. We provide canary/gradual rollout options and automatic fallback to a pinned compatible variant on failures.

00:08:50 Omar: One blocker: our legal team requires proof of encryption with customer-managed keys and a diagram of key flow. how do we show that?
00:09:02 Asha: We'll include the KMS integration diagram showing TOC flows and who manages keys. For Dedicated we support your KMS via BYOK. I'll attach the diagram to the security pack.

00:09:28 Priya: For compliance we also need to know about pen test windows and how to coordinate red-team tests.
00:09:40 Leah: We coordinate pentests; customers can schedule a test with a 2-week notice and we'll provide an IP allowlist and point of contact. For Private/on-prem we provide guidance for air-gapped testing.

00:09:58 Ryan: On the bench plan: we'll ask for a sample traffic trace (Ben to share). We'll run load tests to capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tail behavior, and token throughput for your common prompt sizes. We'll also test scaling during burst traffic.
00:10:15 Ben: i'll sanitize and share a 48h traffic dump with typical session lengths and peak-minute profile. expect that by EOD Friday.

00:10:35 Asha: Great. i'll send SOC2 docs, the security pack link and a pricing estimate.

00:10:50 Omar: Are there any known limitations with large context windows or long sequence KV cache performance? we have some workflows with 8k token contexts.
00:11:05 Ryan: We optimize kernel selection for longer sequences but performance varies; for 8k we recommend the quantization/compile profile we use in our runtime. We'll include a suggested config and expected throughput. Sometimes our internal notes call the runtime the "serve engine" vs "serving runtime" so docs might vary.

00:11:30 Maya: For client SDKs and integration — do you have reference code for streaming chat + stateful session handling?
00:11:42 Leah: Yes, repo links and quickstart templates. we'll share an example that uses prefix caching and session affinity.

00:12:05 Priya: encryption in transit — does Redwood support mTLS between our services and the endpoint?
00:12:18 Ryan: Yes, mTLS supported for Dedicated endpoints. we'll walk through cert rotation and automated renewal patterns.

00:12:42 Ben: Observability — will we get traces for per-request token timing? we want to attribute slow tokens to model vs infra.
00:12:55 Ryan: Console has per-route latency breakdown, token timing traces, and hooks for distributed tracing. we can stream traces to your OTEL backend if desired.

00:13:18 Omar: How do rollouts happen? we want a canary that uses 5% of traffic for 48 hours then 25% then full.
00:13:30 Leah: Rollouts are configurable with canary windows and automatic rollback rules on error/latency regressions. we'll set up a rollout policy in the runbook.

00:13:52 Priya: On data residency — our EU customers' data must remain in eu-west-1. can you guarantee routing by region?
00:14:05 Asha: Yes, we support region routing policies and can pin tenants to eu-west-1 for both Dedicated and Private. For hosted API we have region controls, but Dedicated gives stronger guarantees.

00:14:30 Maya: A couple small things — SDK language support (python/java/node) and example for batching?
00:14:44 Leah: All three supported; we'll include a batching best-practices doc that explains tradeoffs between latency and cost with batching windows.

00:15:05 Ben: Any recommended quantization levels for your runtime that balance p95 and cost?
00:15:17 Ryan: We generally recommend 4-bit for most workloads, 8-bit for especially sensitive quality. We'll include model-specific perf deltas in the benchmark report.

00:15:40 Omar: ok, let's commit to the following: Redwood sends security pack by Apr 1, bench plan by Apr 8, and a pricing/commit proposal by Apr 5. if the bench results meet our p95 targets we'll move forward with a 12-month reserved capacity contract.
00:16:00 Asha: sounds good. i'll follow up with all materials.

00:16:20 Priya: one more question — auditability for model changes. does Redwood retain model version history and who changed what?
00:16:33 Leah: yes, version history and audit trails are part of the console; we keep change events and user IDs and can export them for audits.

00:16:50 Ben: will you provide a demo runbook for our SREs to validate traffic peering before benching?
00:17:03 Ryan: yes, we'll provide a dry-run checklist and pre-bench validation steps.

00:17:25 Asha: quick logistics — i'll share a single zip with security pack, pricing, and the bench plan link: https://redwood.app/s/northstar-onboard. please review and tag questions in the doc.
00:17:45 Omar: noted. we'll loop legal after we see the security pack.

00:18:05 Maya: do you have a sample SLA for Dedicated? we need to compare to our internal vendor bar.
00:18:18 Leah: yes, sample SLA attached in the security pack. typical uptime >99.9 and latency SLOs per model class, plus credits for missed SLOs.

00:18:45 Priya: on encryption key flow - please show the KMS envelope flow, which cloud KMS you tested with. we use AWS KMS.
00:18:58 Ryan: we'll show the AWS KMS flow and how the key is wrapped/unwrapped with our BYOK.

00:19:20 Ben: about scaling - how does autoscaling interact with reserved capacity and burst? are bursts billed differently?
00:19:34 Asha: Reserved capacity covers a baseline throughput. Burst can be configured for short windows; billing has an overage rate or optional burst credits; we'll detail in the pricing doc.

00:19:55 Omar: ok that's helpful. any friction points you usually see during onboarding?
00:20:06 Leah: Mostly around network configs (ACLs, proxy), and sample data shape mismatches for benchmarks. early alignment on traffic samples is the best risk mitigation.

00:20:22 Priya: anything else from Redwood side?
00:20:25 Ryan: we'll confirm bench timing and resource needs after Ben shares the traffic. Also, include any PII markers so we can mask in internal logs during tests.

00:20:40 Ben: i'll mark fields and sanitize and send.

00:20:50 Asha: Great. recap of next steps — (1) security pack by Apr 1, (2) bench plan by Apr 8, (3) pricing by Apr 5, (4) Leah creates onboarding Jira by Mar 30.
00:21:05 Omar: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after the bench results and legal review.

00:21:18 Priya: quick off-topic: do you have references for logistics customers? we prefer peers in the same industry.
00:21:30 Asha: yes, i'll include a redacted reference list and a 1-pager for logistics use-cases.

00:21:45 Leah: i'll set the follow-up demo/workshop to go over the bench outputs and runbook. looking at calendars, week of Apr 12 looks good.

00:22:02 Maya: that works. thanks all.

00:22:12 --- end of substantive discussion; remaining time used for quick Q&A and handoffs ---
00:29:40 Ben: just confirming, who is the technical POC?
00:29:45 Asha: Ryan will be your SE POC and Leah the onboarding lead.
00:30:02 Omar: ok thanks.
00:30:10 Meeting close: thanks everyone — Asha to share artifacts and Leah to send invite for onboarding workspace.
